page.layout: One printed page: running text in one column, with the printed page number and running head at the top. Two marginal notes in the right margin (the first beside the opening of the paragraph on Ionah, the second beside the Lectio entries). Catchword at the foot right, signature at the foot left.

main_text.p: torum maior quàm hominum habenda erat ratio.

Porrò, si æquum est, post lapsum primorum parentum, tot seculis mundi, resAb exemplo omnium creaturarum. creatas uanitati subiici, nō sua sponte, sed propter eum qui subiecit eas isti uanitati: sub spe, quòd & ipsæ uindicabuntur ex seruitute interitus, sic ut unà nobiscum sui spirent & parturiat: Rom. 8.20.21.22. quis intelligens miretur, armentis, pecoribus & iumentis Niniuitarum tempore ieiu-nij & refipiscentiæ ac supplicationum, ali quandiu pabulo potuq; caredum fuisse[?]

Est & illud notandum, ieiunio, operi-mento facci, sefsione in cinere & pulue-re, corpora potissimum affici & macera-ri. Eorum itaq; respectu, bruta minus bene habita, male affici possunt, & homini [illegible, ~12 letters].
main_text.head: VERSVS VIII.

p.i: Operiantur saccis homines ipsi, & ipsa iumenta, atq; clament ad Deum fortiter:Lectio 49. & conuertantur quisq; à uia sua mala, & ab iniquitate quæ est in manibus eorum.7. April.

main_text.p: Inter τὰ πρῶτα[?] secundo loco, habitus lugubris: tertiò, preces: quartò, cōuersio, quæ

page.notes: Greek word after "homini" is not legible on the scan; the word is marked illegible. The Greek after "Inter" is a best reading and is marked [?]. The signature "§ 4" is uncertain. "fuisse" is read from a worn final letter, so it is marked [?]. The printed "Lectio 49." and "7. April." are marginal notes beside the verse.
